 2 weather alerts in effect LIVE: Strong storms hit ArkLaTex on Election Day, damaging winds and flooding possible 
 Storms mostly move through in the morning & midday hours for Election Day 
 By Evan Thomason Published : Nov. 3, 2026 at 4:32 AM CST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SHREVEPORT, La. (KSLA) - We have a round of widespread storms coming throughout the entire ArkLaTex today for Election Day.
 ELECTION DAY STORMS 
 TIMING: 
 Storms hit NE TX, Texarkana, McCurtain County, and SW AR in spots along & north of I-30 from the early morning hours through the mid-morning. 
 Storms move into east TX, Shreveport, and SW AR south of I-30 into the late morning hours mostly between 9 am and noon. 
 Storms move into the rest of NW LA for the lunchtime and early afternoon hours. 
 Storms should be out of the ArkLaTex by the afternoon commute. 
 Cooler for 2nd half of week THREATS: 
 Heavy rainfall is likely within all storms. 
 There is a little chance for flash flooding & strong winds. 
 There is a very low chance for an isolated tornado. 
 Low chance of severe weather COOLER 2ND HALF OF WEEK 
 High temperatures are in the 70s 
 Morning low temperatures drop into the 40s & 50s. 
 Sweater weather coming back RAIN SHOWERS POSSIBLE THURSDAY 
 There is a small chance for a brief rain shower or two on Thursday night or early Friday morning. 
 No severe weather is expected. 
 No severe weather expected BEAUTIFUL WEEKEND AHEAD 
 There is no chance for rain this weekend. 
 Highs are in the low 70s. 
 Morning temperatures are in the 40s. 
 Stay tuned for updates Watch out for the storms today!
 - Meteorologist Evan Thomason
